rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens and earth belong exclusively to God, whose commands and power govern them; no one can resist His limitless power, so people should act under His laws and in His name.
rows.anchor: Bütün semâvât ü arz devlet ve memleketi müstakillen Allah’ın mülküdür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every duty should be done in accord with the rules and enduring order by which God governs His dominion, and for God alone.
rows.anchor: Herkes O’nun için çalışmalı ve her vazifeyi bu mülkü idare eden ahkâm ve evâmirine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation of the heavens and earth and the changing succession of night and day are countless signs of God's ownership, complete power, majesty, and greatness; they benefit people of sound, purified intellect.
rows.anchor: Fakat bu âyetler herkes ve her akıl için değil, temiz ve tam akıl sahipleri demek olan ulü’l-elbâb içindir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens and earth encompass all spatial beings, both higher and lower, implied by the concepts of space.
rows.anchor: Mekân mefhûmunun tazammun ettiği bütün ulviyyât ve süfliyyâtıyla beraber mevcûdât-ı mekâniye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation means bringing beings into and removing them from existence in their essences, attributes, and modes of being, expressing real causation.
rows.anchor: Bunların zât ve sıfatlarıyla bulundukları tarz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The succession and transformation of night and day convey time, relate to motion, and show that created beings are made and ordered.
rows.anchor: Zaman mefhûmunu veren ve harekât ile alâkadar olup bu mevcûdâtın mahlûkiyetlerini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The foundations of true knowledge are discovered by reflecting on the heavens and earth, night and day, creation and alternation, and the meaning of the inner intellect.
rows.anchor: İşte ulûm-i hakkın usûl-i keşfi işbu “semâvât ü arz”, “leyl ü nehâr”, “halk u ihtilâf” ve “lübb” vâkı‘ât

rows.speaker: Ubeyd b. Umeyr
rows.claim: Ubeyd b. Umeyr recounts that Aisha described the Prophet's extraordinary night worship: he sought permission to pray, wept during prayer, and said he should be a grateful servant despite forgiveness.
rows.anchor: radıyallâhu anh hazretleri demiştir ki: “Hazret-i Âişe’ye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the report from Aisha, the Prophet warns that woe awaits whoever recites this revelation without reflecting on it; another wording likens recitation without reflection to chewing it in the jaws.
rows.anchor: Vay bunu okuyup da bu babda tefekkür etmeyene!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel in 2:164 gives eight kinds of proof for divine unity in fuller detail, while this verse condenses their basis and develops it toward spiritual progress.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Bakara’da vahdâniyet-i ilâhiyeyi isbat ve takrir siyâkında bu âyetin bir nazîri geçmiş idi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording shifts from signs for people who reason in 2:164 to signs for people of inner intellect here: initial proof of unity needs reason, while progress in knowledge of God calls for a purified intellect.
rows.anchor: Bunun için onun nihâyetinde لاَٰيَاتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ [2/164] bunda da لَءَايَٰتٍۢ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ buyurulmuş

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi says a seeker first needs many proofs, but once the heart is lit by knowledge of God, fewer, summarized proofs help it avoid distraction and deepen contemplation; he connects this to Moses being told to remove his sandals (20:12).
rows.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî hazretleri bu terakki nokta-i nazarından der ki: “Sâlik ilallâha evvelemirde teksîr-i delâil lâzımdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In summary, the earlier passage seeks a journey toward God, whereas this passage seeks progress through God; the earlier follows the assertion of divine unity in 2:163, while this follows God's sovereignty in 3:189.
rows.anchor: Hulâsa orada “seyr ilallah” matlub idi, burada ise “seyr billâh” matlubdur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present reflection concerns the manifestation and governance of God's kingdom and the purpose of creation; it is suited to mature minds and believing hearts refined by transmitted and rational knowledge and advanced in worship and knowledge.
rows.anchor: Bu da ma‘ârif-i akliye ve nakliye ile tehzib olunmuş ve vahdâniyet-i ilâhiyeye iman ile ubûdiyet ve marifette kat‘-ı merâhil etmiş ukūl-i kâmile ve kulûb-ı mü’mine erbâbının kârı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's guaranteed acceptance of repentance is for people who commit wrong through ignorance, then repent soon and do not persist in the sin.
rows.anchor: sonra çok geçmeden tevbe eden, günahında ısrar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance is not promised for those who repeatedly commit wrong and wait until death arrives before saying they repent, nor for those who die as disbelievers.
rows.anchor: bir de kâfir olarak ölenlere tevbe yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For deliberate sinners who do not repent soon and make sin habitual, but repent before the death throes and despair of life, acceptance is possible by God's will but is not certain.
rows.anchor: bilerek günah yapan çok geçmeden tevbe etmeyip seyyiâtı itiyad eden ve ma‘amâfîh hâlet-i nez‘e gelip hayattan meyus olmadan evvel tevbe edenlerin tevbelerinin kabûlü kat‘î değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith adopted before the death throes, while a person still hopes to live, is accepted; faith adopted in despair during the death throes is not.
rows.anchor: hâlet-i nez‘den önce henüz hayattan meyus olmazdan evvel küfürden tevbe ile iman makbuldür. Fakat hâlet-i nez‘de yeis hâlinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A new believer needs time after faith to acquire good deeds.
rows.anchor: İmandan sonra amel-i hayr kesbedebilecek bir zaman bulunmalıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sinful believer's repentance at the last breath may be accepted, as in the call not to despair of God's mercy (39:53), but acceptance is still not guaranteed.
rows.anchor: mü’min-i fâsıkın son nefesindeki tevbesi de makbul olabilir. لَا تَقْنَطُوا۟ مِن رَّحْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ’dır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet does not claim independent or delegated control of God's stores; sending signs or punishment and granting worldly wealth belong to God, so people cannot demand prosperity as proof of his mission.
rows.anchor: ben “Allah’ın kudret hazineleri bendedir, bana tefviz olunmuştur, ben onlarda istiklâlen veya isti’zânen dilediğim gibi tasarruf ederim” demem

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hazā'in is the plural of khizāna, a protected storehouse where wealth is kept beyond ordinary reach.
rows.anchor: “Hazâin”; lisânımızda “hazine” veya “hazne” tâbir olunan “hizâne”nin cem‘idir ki, ellerin erişemeyeceği bir surette mal iddihar olunan muhrez mekânın ismidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet does not claim knowledge of what is hidden from him or practice divination; therefore questions about the Hour or the timing of punishment are misplaced, as 7:188 also says.
rows.anchor: Ben gaybı da bilmem: İlmimden gāib bulunan ef‘âl ve ma‘lûmât-ı ilâhiyeyi bilirim diye iddia da etmem; kehanet taslamam.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet does not claim to be an angel; people cannot demand extraordinary angel-like acts such as ascending to heaven (17:93), or use ordinary human eating and walking to deny his prophethood (25:7).
rows.anchor: Ben size “Bir meleğim” de demem, bir melek olduğumu da iddia etmem.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He follows only what is revealed; his reports about the unseen come from revelation and convey God's knowledge rather than his own independent knowledge.
rows.anchor: ancak bana gönderilen vahye uyarım, ona tâbi‘olurum.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: According to 72:26–27, God reveals the unseen to no one except a chosen, trusted messenger, whom He guards and informs of some unseen matters.
rows.anchor: Allah gaybına hiç kimseyi muttali‘ve hâkim kılmaz. Ancak ihtiyar ettiği ve emin kıldığı resul müstesnâdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once disclosed by revelation, an unseen report is known as reported unseen, not absolute unseen; human knowledge consists in signs and reports entering the heart, not the things themselves.
rows.anchor: Bunun içindir ki ilm-i beşerin hepsi bir haber, bir kaziyye mahiyetinde tecellî eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation is God's speech forcefully entering the heart; prophethood is receiving revelation and acting on it, so the Prophet sees and reports God's signs and is a proof to those who have not heard.
rows.anchor: Vahiy de kelâmullah olan âyât-ı Hakk’ın kalbe nüfûz-ı cebrîsidir. Risalet de Allah’tan vahiy telakkī etmek ve muktezâsıyla amel eylemekten ibarettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The difference between prophets and others resembles that between sighted people and the blind: those who cannot see benefit by hearing a witness, and ordinary people similarly benefit from prophets.
rows.anchor: Ve peygamberlerle peygamber olmayanların farkı gözlülerle a‘mâların farkı gibidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warn those who fear being gathered to their Lord, whether they believe in the gathering or merely consider it possible; they have no protector or intercessor apart from God, and may thereby become God-fearing.
rows.anchor: kalblerinde böyle bir haşr korkusu, bir âhiret hissi bulunduğu hâlde korunmayan veya korunmasını bilmeyen gayr-i muttakīleri inzar eyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who categorically deny the afterlife, or are certain that idols, ancestors, spiritual masters, or unauthorized prophets will rescue them, cannot be reached by this warning; those who allow they lack other protectors can be moved by it.
rows.anchor: Allah’tan başka velî ve şefî‘leri olmadığına inanan veya ihtimal verenler kābil-i inzar ve teessürdürler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must not expel people who worship their Lord morning and evening, continually seeking God's presence and favor with sincere, exclusive devotion.
rows.anchor: sabah akşam, yani her zaman Rablerine dua ve ibadet ederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither their reckoning belongs to the Prophet nor his reckoning to them; he must not expel them on the pretext of accounting for them.
rows.anchor: Onların hesaplarından hiçbir şey sana ait değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Expelling these worshippers would make the Prophet one of the wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: ki zâlimlerden olursun.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı reports that Quraysh leaders asked Muhammad to remove poor Muslims such as Suhayb, Khabbāb, Bilāl, ʿAmmār, and Salmān so they might visit; after Umar urged trying it and they pressed for a written promise, the verse was revealed and the Prophet discarded the page.
rows.anchor: Rivayet olunuyor ki Kureyş’in ileri gelenlerinden birtakımları Hazret-i Peygamber’e uğramışlar

rows.speaker: Selmân ve Habbâb
rows.claim: Salmān and Khabbāb say the verse concerned them: the Prophet sat close with them and would not leave before they did; after 18:28, he stayed with them and thanked God for the command.
rows.anchor: radıyallahu anhümâ demişlerdir ki: “Bu âyet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tests one group through another: arrogant elites scorn poor, sincere believers as undeserving, while faith and sincerity are divine gifts that challenge worldly pride and status.
rows.anchor: bir fitne ile yani tard ü istihkāra şâyan zannedilen fukara ve zu‘afâyı iman ve ihlâs ile memnun ve muazzez etmek gibi bir imtihan iledir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those tested who recognize that gifts come from God, submit humbly, and repent succeed; those whose pride intensifies and who deny others' virtue and contest God's decree begin to fall into deep ruin.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın dilediğine dilediğini vermekte bulunduğunu anlayarak acz-i ubûdiyetlerini idrâk eder ve Hakk’a teslîm-i nefs edip tevbekâr olurlarsa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The test has many forms, but its chief form is that poor and weak people receive faith and sincerity while prosperous, proud people persist in disbelief and lack of piety; this explains the ban on expelling them.
rows.anchor: bu imtihanın suver-i muhtelifesi bulunmakla beraber başı ve en mühimi mağrûr-ı ikbâl olanların küfr ü fıskına ve ittikāsızlığına mukabil fukara ve zu‘afâya Allah’a iman ve ihlâs nimetinin bahşedilmesidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows best who is grateful, contrary to the proud people's dismissal of sincere worshippers as unworthy of divine favor.
rows.anchor: onlardan ve herkesten a‘lem değil midir?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After directing the Prophet to offer believers glad tidings, the author says God elaborates the signs in keeping with the detailed exposition already given.
rows.anchor: tâ yukarılardan beri gelen tafsîlât-ı bedî‘a ile

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God explains the signs in detail so the way of the guilty becomes clear; on the reading سبيلُ, the Prophet is to clarify and cut off the criminals' path.
rows.anchor: mücrimler yolu tamamen tebeyyün etmek için -سَبِيلُ kıraatine göre- mücrimlerin yolunu senin tavzih ettirmen, kesip atman içindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disjointed letters are whose purpose God knows; Ibn Abbas is reported to read them as “I am Allah, knowing and explaining,” while Suddi takes Ṣād as a shortened form of al-Muṣawwir.
rows.anchor: Ezcümle İbn Abbas’tan bir rivayete göre أَنَا االلهُ أَعْلَمُ وَأُفَ ِّصلُ “Ben Allahım, bilir ve tafsil ederim” demek olduğu nakledilmiştir.

rows.speaker: Süddî
rows.claim: Suddi proposes that Ṣād is an abbreviated form of al-Muṣawwir.
rows.anchor: Süddî اَلْمُصَ ِّورُ muhaffefi olduğunu

rows.speaker: بعضى
rows.claim: Some suggest the letters refer to “Have We not expanded your breast?” and “We destroyed it”; the author says such conjectures lack a fixed linguistic basis and should not be relied on.
rows.anchor: bazıları اَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ صَدْرَكَ أَهْلَكْنَٰهَا mânasına olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because arbitrary interpretations without established linguistic usage could be multiplied endlessly, exegetes say they cannot be relied upon, though Ibn Abbas's reading merits attention from the context between the two surahs.
rows.anchor: elfâzın lisanda bir vaz‘-ı mahsûsuna istinad etmeyen bu gibi ihtimâlâtın binlercesi hatıra gelebileceğinden, müfessirîn bunlara itimad câiz olamayacağını beyan ederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like the openings of al-Baqara and Āl ʿImrān, these letters signal realities and symbolic meanings beyond full human comprehension, as stated in 3:7; believers should admit their limits and submit.
rows.anchor: bu sûrede dahi künh-i hakikatini daha ziyade bir tafsil ile ihâta edemeyeceğimiz birtakım hakāik-i îmâniye karşısında i‘tirâf-ı acz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matters of creation's beginning, moral responsibility, the afterlife, prophetic miracles, and seeing God are examples of such realities.
rows.anchor: Ezcümle mebde’-i hilkat, sırr-ı teklif, ahvâl-i âhiret, mu‘cizât-ı enbiyâ, rü’yetullah mesâili bu kabîldendir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation is a book sent to Muhammad: he should not doubt its divine origin or be distressed by the importance and difficulty of his mission.
rows.anchor: Yani bunun Allah’tan münzel olduğunda şekkin olmadığı gibi, sana teklif ettiği vazifenin fevkalâde ehemmiyet ve müşkilâtından dolayı da sıkılma.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For unbelievers the Quran warns of a fearful end; for believers it recalls truths they may have forgotten and should guide their choices as a continual reminder.
rows.anchor: Mü’minler Kur’ân’ı dâimî bir muhtıra, bir rehber olmak üzere ellerinde ve gönüllerinde tutmalı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who do not benefit from the Quran may exist, but no one escapes its judgment; rejecting its warning, including the curse on disbelievers in 2:89, puts one under that warning.
rows.anchor: lâkin Kur’ân’ın hükmünden hâriç kalabilecek hiç kimse tasavvur edilemez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People must follow what God revealed and no human or jinn friend, helper, or authority independently; the revealed book is the measure for deciding whose words and actions to follow.
rows.anchor: gerek ins ve gerek cinden herhangi bir dostun, bir zahîrin, bir veliyyü’l-emrin bizzat kendilerine ve kendiliklerinden olan kavil veya fiillerine tâbi‘oluvermeyiniz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many towns were struck suddenly at night while residents slept or by day during their rest; the people admitted they had been wrongdoers only after punishment had arrived, too late to escape.
rows.anchor: ya kavm-i Lût gibi gece yarısında veya kavm-i Şuayb gibi güpe gündüz hâl-i istirâhat ü gaflette azab kendilerini bastırıverdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will question all peoples to whom messengers were sent about how they answered those messengers, as in 28:65.
rows.anchor: kendilerine peygamber gönderilmiş olanlara elbette ve elbette

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will also question all the messengers about how people responded, as in 5:109.
rows.anchor: ve gönderilmiş olan bütün peygamberlere de elbette

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There are two kinds of questioning: a rebuke and accounting, and a request to learn; the questioning here is censure of unbelievers before the messengers.
rows.anchor: İki nevi sual vardır. Birisi tevbih ve muâhaze suâlidir. Nitekim bu mâna ile lisânımızda “iyi belle bunu ben sana sorarım” denilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statements that sinners will not be questioned in 55:39 and 28:78 mean their guilt is already evident from their faces and recorded evidence, so inquiry is unnecessary.
rows.anchor: mücrimiyetleri sîmâlarından belli, cürümleri bütün vesâikiyle mâlum ve mazbuttur. Kendilerinden veya şundan bundan sormaya hâcet yoktur demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When messengers are asked, they will say they have no knowledge and that God knows the unseen (5:109); God will then recount every hidden and public deed, since He was never absent.
rows.anchor: bunun üzerine en gizli hâllerine varıncaya kadar hepsinin yaptıklarını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will fully recount events with knowledge because He witnessed every outward and inward act and was never absent.
rows.anchor: biz gāib değil idik ki mâlumumuz olmayan bir hâlleri bulunabilsin, zâhir ve bâtında her ne yaptılarsa Allah hepsine hâzır ve nâzır ve şâhiddir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weighing on that Day is real, fully just, and exact: unlike the partial accounting or respite before then, every deed and every balance of credit and debt will be measured and accounts closed.
rows.anchor: O gün ise defter-i a‘mâldeki her muâmele en ince, en hurde noktalarına varıncaya kadar bihakkın tartılıp leh ve aleyhteki matlub ve zimmetin muvâzeneleri tamamen tahakkuk edecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural “scales” indicates that each individual has multiple scales, with the final result calculated from their combined total.
rows.anchor: Cemi‘sîgasıyla مَوَٰزِينُهُۥ tâbirinden anlaşılır ki her ferd için bile müte‘addid mîzanlar vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whose good deeds, credits, and profits outweigh their sins, debts, and losses are the truly successful.
rows.anchor: hasenâtı seyyiâtından, matlubları zimmetlerinden, kârları zararlarından fazla çıkarsa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with light scales have ruined themselves because they persistently deny God's signs and refuse to give them their due.
rows.anchor: bunun sebebi bizim âyetlerimize zulm eder olmaları müstemirren tekzib ve inkâr ve hakkını vermekten imtinâ‘edegelmeleridir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adornments God brings forth include clothing made from plants, animals, and minerals, while wholesome provisions include every pleasant, clean food and drink; no one has authority to forbid these by personal fiat.
rows.anchor: kısmet olup lezzet ü iştihâ ile intifâ‘edilecek, hoş hoş, temiz temiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes that food, clothing, and forms of adornment are presumptively permitted.
rows.anchor: bu âyet, mat‘ûmât ve melbûsât ve envâ‘-ı tecemmülâtta asl olan ibâha olduğuna delildir.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas ve birçok müfessirîn
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and many exegetes interpret “adornment” as clothing.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas ve birçok müfessirîn “ziynet”i melbûsât ile tefsir etmişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation includes every kind of adornment so long as it is not extravagant; the author says this is the apparent meaning, including bodily grooming, mounts, and all jewelry.
rows.anchor: Fakat diğer bir kavle göre israf olmamak üzere envâ‘-ı tezyînâtın hepsine şâmildir ki zâhiri de budur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gold, silver, and silk for men would fall under the general permission if a Prophetic hadith had not specifically prohibited them.
rows.anchor: Eğer hadîs-i nebevîde erkek için altın ve gümüş ve ipeğin hurmeti hakkında bilhassa nas vârid olmamış olsa idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are the true beneficiaries of these provisions: unbelievers share them only secondarily in this life, while the afterlife reserves them for believers alone.
rows.anchor: Fakat bu hayât-ı dünyâda kâfirler dahi ona velev bi’t-teba‘olsun iştirak ederler. Fakat yevm-i kıyâmette onlar yalnız bu dünyadaki mü’minlere mahsus olacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forbids every indecency, public or hidden, especially sexual immorality; examples of hidden indecency are relations with a prohibited spouse or resuming relations after irrevocable divorce without a new marriage.
rows.anchor: Meselâ nikâhı câiz olmayanı nikâh etmek, talâk-ı bâinden sonra tecdîd-i nikâh edilmeden zevciyet muâmelesini devam ettirmek gizli fuhşiyyât cümlesindendir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forbids sin in general, every act contrary to reason and religious law, especially intoxicants and drunkenness.
rows.anchor: akl ü şer‘a muhalif her kötü fiili

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forbids unjust aggression that violates the rights to life, property, honor, and dignity; “without right” clarifies and reinforces the wrongfulness, since rightful aggression is a contradiction.
rows.anchor: bi-gayr-i hak bağyi haddini tecavüzle cana, mala, ırza, yani haysiyet ü hukūka ta‘addî ve zulmü.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Associating partners with God has no revealed proof or rational warrant; it is ignorant desire and a greater prohibition than indecency, sin, or aggression.
rows.anchor: bütün âlem bir Allah’a delil olduğu hâlde Allah’a şirk koşmak için ilmî bir sultası olacak hiçbir burhan, hiçbir delil yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also forbids claiming without knowledge that He commanded something, or inventing religious rulings through ignorance and unbelief.
rows.anchor: Allah’a karşı ilminiz olmayan şeyi söylemenizi, وَٱللَّهُ أَمَرَنَا بِهَا dediğiniz gibi cehalet ve ilhad ile yalan söyleyerek din ve ahkâm uydurmaya kalkmanızı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God explains these signs for people of knowledge, who infer and apply the meanings contained within them.
rows.anchor: Artık ehl-i ilim bunların zımnındaki mânaları istinbat eder anlar, ona göre tatbik ve istifade ederler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each community, nation, state, and even individual has an appointed period of respite before punishment or destruction; different wrongdoing may take different lengths of time to bring an end.
rows.anchor: Ümem-i muhtelifeden her birine ve hatta her ümmetten her ferde mahsus bir ecel, bir gāye-i müddet vardır.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas ve ekser müfessirînin muhtârı
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas's and most exegetes' preferred reading takes the appointed term here as the time for punishment or destruction, not a person's lifespan; thus a righteous community may endure until the world's end.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas ve ekser müfessirînin muhtârına göre bu âyetteki “ecel”, siyâka nazaran mutlak ömür mânasına olmayıp ecel-i azâb ve helâk demek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the appointed time comes, no one can delay or advance it even by a moment; only God knows its timing, so people should not be deceived by temporary respite but repent and obey promptly.
rows.anchor: Bu müddeti ise ancak Allah bilir. Binâen‘aleyh bir müddet cereyan eden bu müsaadeye mağrur olup da ilâ gayri’n-nihâye böyle gidecek zannetmemeli

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about ten wealthy Quraysh who funded the Battle of Badr, each slaughtering ten camels daily to feed their army; it also foretells further spending in later battles such as Uhud.
rows.anchor: Bu âyet Bedir Muharebesi için mallarını sarf eden, ezcümle her biri yevmiye on deve keserek askerlerini it‘âm eden on Kureyş zengini hakkında nâzil olmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers spend to block God's path; the money will become a source of regret, and although fortunes in battle may alternate, they will ultimately be decisively defeated by truth.
rows.anchor: sonra o mallar kendilerine bir hasret olacak boşuna telef edilmiş, hevâya sarf olunmuş bulunduğunu anlayacak, “eyvah!” diyecekler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who persist in disbelief will be gathered and driven to Hell.
rows.anchor: ve küfredenler sırf cehenneme sevk edilecekler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God separates good from evil so the promised distinction for the pious is realized and the good and bad become clearly distinct.
rows.anchor: Allah habîsi tayyibden ayırsın. Müttakīlere mev‘ud olan furkan hâsıl olsun, iyiler kötülerden temayüz etsin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God piles the evil together, adds their evil wealth to them, heaps it all up densely, and casts the whole into Hell; these are the losers.
rows.anchor: habis kısmını birbirinin üzerine bindirip habis mallarını kendilerine zammedip

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the unbelievers stop fighting and submit to the truth, their past sins will be forgiven; if they return to war, they should expect the same fate as earlier peoples who opposed their prophets, with Badr as a sufficient example.
rows.anchor: bulundukları hâli bırakıp hakka teslîm-i nefs ederlerse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's decree that He and His messengers will prevail, and that righteous servants inherit the earth, supports the warning if unbelievers return to hostility.
rows.anchor: Bunlar misâl-i kâfîdir. Binâen‘aleyh dönüp onların yolunu tutarlar, onların âdetine sülûk ederlerse
